data.name: Frank
data.long_meaning: Derived from Old Germanic 'Frank' meaning 'free', 'frank' or 'open'. In history, the Franks were a Germanic tribe, and the term 'Frank' referred to a free person, a member of the tribe, or a free peasant. The name Frank is also associated with the idea of being honest, straight-forward, and open.

in_hebrew.name: פרנק
in_hebrew.meaning: פירוש השם הוא חופשי או ללא עול
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם פרנק מקורו בשם העברי פרנקוס, שפירושו חופשי או ללא עול. הוא קשור לשם של שבט גרמאני שנקרא פרנקים, שפירושו 'חופשי' או 'פתוח'. השם משמש גם כקיצור לשם פרנציסקוס, שפירושו איש צרפת או חופשי מצרפת. השם פרנק מופיע גם בכתבי הקודש הנוצריים כפרנקוס, שפירושו 'אדם חופשי'.

in_greek.name: Φρανκ
in_greek.meaning: Το όνομα σημαίνει ελεύθερος ή χωρίς βάρος
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Φρανκ προέρχεται από το γερμανικό όνομα Frank, που σημαίνει ελεύθερος ή χωρίς βάρος. Οι Φράνκοι ήταν γερμανική φυλή που λεγόταν έτσι επειδή ήταν ελεύθεροι και ανεξάρτητοι. Το όνομα συνδέεται επίσης με το όνομα Φραγκίσκος, που σημαίνει άνθρωπος από τη Γαλλία ή ελεύθερος από τη Γαλλία. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, το όνομα Frank δεν αναφέρεται άμεσα, αλλά η έννοια της ελευθερίας είναι κεντρική στη διδασκαλία του Χριστού.

in_latin.name: Francus

In early Christian tradition, the concept of freedom is central to the teachings of Christ, and the name Frank reflects this value.

historical_references.reference: The Franks were a Germanic people who lived in the eastern part of the Frankish territories, in the region that is now Belgium and Luxembourg. They became one of the most powerful tribes in the late Roman Empire. Clovis I, a Frankish king, was the first Christian king of the Franks and converted to Christianity in 496 AD.
historical_references.context: Clovis I, the son of Childeric I, was the first Christian king of the Franks. He converted to Christianity after his victory in the Battle of Tolbiac against the Alamanni. This battle marked the end of the Roman influence in this part of Europe and the beginning of the Frankish domination.

historical_references.reference: Charlemagne, also known as Charles the Great, was the King of the Franks from 768 to 814 AD. He is considered to be the father of Europe because of his efforts to unite and strengthen the Frankish Empire. Charlemagne was also a devout Christian, and he played an important role in spreading Christianity throughout his empire.
historical_references.context: Charlemagne was the son of Pepin the Short and was crowned King of the Franks in 768 AD at the age of 21. He expanded the Frankish Empire by conquering lands in Germany and Italy, and he also established the Carolingian dynasty, which ruled Europe until the 14th century. Charlemagne was a strong supporter of Christianity, and he made it the state religion of the Frankish Empire. He also founded numerous monasteries and supported scholars, leading to the Carolingian Renaissance.
